question: Does sampling all receiver pixels instead of a fixed1024 per map let the full-terrain network learn transferable propagation structure?
evidence: On four FIT terrains, dense vs fixed coverage improved untouched-pixel RMSE .667/.695dB after matched4000updates; dense beats frozenC38 by .173/.280dB. This is not unseen-terrain validation.
shared: C61path model; same dense-fourFIT warm encoder with output heads zeroed; all5508FITterrains/23158maps; seed20261210;16maps x256points;6000updates;AdamW.0005wd1e-4;cosine,warm200; stop >=4000 and patience2000.
features: Arbitrary-pixel pipeline matches original294 features max4.58e-6, C38prediction RMSdifference .000238/.000345dB on4096knownpoints; input-only.
evaluation: Unchanged sampledDEV612 (256points/map), minimum mean band RMSE selection; full-map DEV check only if both >=.15dB gain. OfficialVAL excluded from gradients/selection.
limits: One seed. Common stopping rule may end at different steps; compare shared steps as well. FITmonitor pixels are not heldout.
